rv.q: This show, like the painting, is beautiful.
LaChanze's production is spirited, brilliantly executed, and simply phenomenal on all counts.
As this new production potently demonstrates, the time is now for Wine in the Wilderness .

It is a beautiful piece of writing, and in LaChanze’s clever direction and her excellent company of actors’ hands it is freshly transformed—nearly sixty years after it was written—into a drama that, while rooted in the past, feels current and urgent.
“Wine in the Wilderness” advises we all do the same, with a wit and beauty that are fully served in this must-see production.
Resurrecting the role of Tommy—especially with Washington’s electrifying performance—is a gift to today’s audience in understanding the evolution of the Black woman in American history.
This is a finely aged Wine , ready for uncorking and more pouring in future productions.
In no way does she let Childress down, but this mounting merely skims the surface, much like the first two panels of Bill’s magnum opus.
Not all of LaChanze’s production is so acute.
The entire cast is wonderful, and Olivia Washington (West End's Slave Play ) is spellbinding as the two faces of Tommy, who Bill gradually comprehends as one complex human being.
Seeing Alice Childress’s work back on the New York stage is a gift.

cn.t: Critics hail this exquisite revival of Childress' neglected 1969 play as essential viewing, with Olivia Washington delivering an electrifying performance. LaChanze's directorial debut brings vivid life to a smart exploration of Black identity and womanhood.

vr.q: I thought this was a really great production.
